fine_lines.title: faint vs pass out
fine_lines.explanation_ar: faint كلمة طبية تعني الإغماء عندما لا يصل الدم إلى المخ بشكل كافٍ (مثلاً عند رؤية الدم أو هبوط السكر). pass out لها استخدامان: الأول نفس معنى faint لكن بشكل غير رسمي، والثاني مجازي: أن ينام شخص فوراً من شدة الإرهاق كأنه فقد الوعي.

examples.sentence: He fainted because his blood sugar was low.
After 16 hours of work, she passed out on the sofa.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Faint" is a medical word for suddenly losing consciousness when not enough blood reaches the brain (for example, when seeing blood or with low blood sugar). "Pass out" has two uses: first, the same meaning as "faint" but informal; second, to fall asleep immediately because you are extremely tired, as if you lost consciousness.

fine_lines.title: sip vs gulp
fine_lines.explanation_ar: sip أن تشرب ببطء كميات صغيرة جداً (رشفة)، كما نفعل مع الشاي أو القهوة الساخنة أو مشروب نستمتع به. gulp أن تبلع كميات كبيرة بسرعة، كما يفعل العطشان جداً بعد التمرين.

examples.sentence: She gulped down a whole bottle of water.

fine_lines.explanation_en: To "sip" is to drink slowly in very small amounts, as we do with hot tea or coffee or a drink we enjoy. To "gulp" is to swallow large amounts quickly, as a very thirsty person does after exercise.

fine_lines.title: cappuccino vs latte
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنان إسبريسو مع حليب ورغوة. الكابتشينو فيه رغوة أكثر (تقريباً ثلث إسبريسو وثلث حليب وثلث رغوة)، أما اللاتيه ففيه حليب أكثر ورغوة أقل.

examples.sentence: I like the thick foam on my cappuccino.
A latte is milder because it has more milk.

fine_lines.explanation_en: Both are espresso with milk and foam. A cappuccino has more foam (about one third espresso, one third milk, one third foam), while a latte has more milk and less foam.

fine_lines.title: lemonade vs lemon juice
fine_lines.explanation_ar: lemon juice هو عصير الليمون الصافي بعد عصره مباشرة. lemonade هي الليموناضة المحلّاة بالسكر والماء أو إضافات أخرى تقلّل حموضتها. إذا أردت مشروباً فاطلب lemonade.

examples.sentence: A glass of cold lemonade, please.
Add a spoon of lemon juice to the salad.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Lemon juice" is the pure juice that comes out when you squeeze a lemon. "Lemonade" is a drink made sweeter with sugar and water or other things that make it less sour. If you want something to drink, ask for lemonade.

grammar.title: Present perfect continuous: focus on the process
grammar.explanation_ar: المضارع التام المستمر (have/has been + فعل+ing) يركّز على العملية والمجهود والوقت المستهلك، لا على النتيجة. المضارع التام البسيط «شهادة إتمام»: انظر ماذا أنجزت. أما المستمر فهو «الورشة»: انظر كم تعبت وما زلت في وسط العمل. والـ ing هي صوت الماكينة التي ما زالت تعمل.
examples: I've painted the house. (It's finished and beautiful.)
I've been painting the house. (Look at my clothes! I'm tired.)
Have you been running? You look tired.
grammar.explanation_en: The present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) focuses on the process, the effort and the time spent, not the result. The simple present perfect is like a "certificate": look what I finished. The continuous is like a "workshop": look how hard I've been working, and I'm still in the middle of it. The -ing is the sound of a machine that is still running.

grammar.title: Numbers mean a finished result
grammar.explanation_ar: عندما تذكر رقماً أو كمية منجزة (50 صفحة، 3 أكواب) فأنت تتكلم عن نتيجة، فاستخدم المضارع التام البسيط. وعندما تريد إظهار التعب والمدة فاستخدم المستمر.
examples: I've been reading all day, and my eyes hurt.
She has cooked dinner. / She has been cooking all morning.
grammar.explanation_en: When you give a number or a finished amount (50 pages, 3 cups), you are talking about a result, so use the simple present perfect. When you want to show effort and how long something took, use the continuous.

grammar.title: Polite ways to order
grammar.explanation_ar: تجنّب صيغة الأمر المباشر عند الطلب من النادل. Bring me... أسوأ الطرق، و I want... غير مهذبة، و I'll take... مقبولة. الأفضل: Could I have ..., please?
examples: Could I have a cappuccino, please?
Can I get a smoothie, please?
I'd like an iced tea, please.
grammar.explanation_en: Avoid giving direct orders to a waiter. "Bring me..." is the worst way, "I want..." is not polite, and "I'll take..." is OK. The best is: Could I have ..., please?

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to order?
choices: Could I have a coffee, please?
questions.explanation_ar: Could I have ..., please? هي الصيغة المهذبة الأفضل.
questions.explanation_en: "Could I have ..., please?" is the best polite form.
